sensors.name: left light sensor (LLIGHT), the light from above

control_flow: driveInTheDark: if LLIGHT is less than 30 %, drive forward at 30 %; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

decision_points.condition: the left light sensor reads less than 30 %

branches.reason: The light inside a tunnel never falls below 40 %, so a reading below 30 % never happens in the simulator.
branches.outcome: darker than 30 %: it drives forward at 30 %
30 % or brighter: it checks the obstacle sensor

decision_points.condition: an obstacle is ahead (obstacle sensor FRONT)

branches.outcome: an obstacle is ahead: it stops
no obstacle: it follows the line

input_dimensions.dimension: where the robot starts relative to the line
what is ahead on the line

scenarios.coded_response: The light is 40 % there, not below 30 %: it takes the bright branch, finds no obstacle and follows the line until it ends, then curves right into the tunnel wall
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a line in bright light; the line runs into a tunnel and ends a little inside it
scenarios.trigger: The robot comes into the dim light under the roof and the line ends
scenarios.title: Gets through the tunnel
assumptions: You didn't say whether a line runs on through the tunnel: the line ends a little inside it, and the robot should go on without the line.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It drives on through the tunnel and reaches its far part, without bumping into the walls

scenarios.coded_response: It stops and keeps stopping while the wall is ahead
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a line in bright light, with a wall across the line ahead
scenarios.trigger: The obstacle sensor sees the wall
scenarios.title: Stops before a wall
assumptions: You didn't say it should stop at walls, but your program does.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops in front of the wall without bumping into it

uncertainties: Your program drives forward only when the light is below 30 %, but inside a tunnel the light never falls below 40 %: that part never runs.
On a plain floor the program turns right and circles, so it needs a line to get anywhere.
When the line ends under the roof it finds no black, curves right and bumps into the tunnel wall.

tests.name: Follows the line into the tunnel and gets through it
tests.scenario: Given the robot starts on a line that runs into a tunnel, when the program runs, then it drives on through the dark inside the tunnel and reaches Goal 1 in its far part without bumping into the walls.

equivalence_partitions.dimension: where the robot starts relative to the line

expected_results: It follows the line into the tunnel and keeps going in the dark, reaching Goal 1 in the tunnel's far part.

postconditions.description: By the end of the run, the robot has touched Goal 1 inside the tunnel.
During the whole run, it never bumps into the tunnel's walls.
